records.title: Backend authentication configuration is centralized in Settings

source.revision: current working-tree snapshot; git revision unavailable

records.evidence: backend/app/core/config.py defines a shared Pydantic BaseSettings instance, reads ../.env and environment variables, and declares SECRET_KEY, ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES (8 days), EMAIL_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRE_HOURS (48 hours), SMTP/sender settings, and initial-superuser settings. backend/app/core/security.py hardcodes JWT algorithm HS256 and uses SECRET_KEY. backend/app/api/routes/login.py applies the access-token lifetime; backend/app/utils.py creates/verifies reset tokens and sends email using these settings.
records.claim: Backend authentication and password-reset configuration is centralized in backend/app/core/config.py and exposed through the shared settings instance. It reads environment variables and ../.env. Access tokens use required SECRET_KEY and have a default lifetime of 8 days; password-reset tokens default to 48 hours. SMTP settings optionally enable recovery email. JWT algorithm HS256 is hardcoded in backend/app/core/security.py, not a configurable setting.
records.rationale: This compact source-linked map is reusable for future questions about backend authentication configuration and avoids rediscovering the settings definition and the code paths that consume its key values.
